 33|“우선 앉으시죠.”

 80|
 81|“그렇습니까.”

100|
101|하지만 뼈가 있는 최 팀장의 말에도 후긴은 미소를 잃지 않았다.
102|
103|“아, 직접 오시지 못한 것에 대해서도 매우 안타까워하셨습니다.”
104|
105|“길드장님께서 많이 바쁘신가 보군요. 제가 아는 바에 의하면 그분께서도 외부 활동을 끊으신 지 벌써 수년째라고 하던데…… 역시 소문은 믿을 게 못 되는 것 같습니다.”
106|
107|지위가 높은 사람일수록 엉덩이가 무거워지는 건 만고불변의 진리다.

111|대부분의 거대 길드장들은 외부와의 접촉을 삼갔고, 그것은 오딘 길드장 역시 마찬가지였다.

113|“그렇지 않아도 평소에 존경하던 분이라 한번 찾아뵙고 인사를 드리고 싶은데, 어떻게 생각하십니까?”

115|“하하, 글쎄요.”

117|소리 내어 웃은 후긴이 깍지를 끼며 말을 이었다.

121|“무언가 일이 생긴 모양입니다.”

125|“다른 분들이라면?”

132|
133|“크로노스 길드라.”

135|“부디 못 들은 것으로 해 주셨으면 합니다. 그렇지 않아도 종종 이런 실수를 저질러서 길드장님께 불려 가 질책을 듣곤 하거든요.”
136|
137|곤란한 표정을 짓는 후긴의 모습에, 나는 참지 못하고 피식 웃었다.
138|
139|“실수는 무슨.”
140|
141|“네?”
142|
143|“거기 까마귀 아저씨. 어쭙잖은 발연기는 이제 집어치우고, 지금부터는 좀 진솔한 대화를 나눠 봅시다.”

145|음. 그냥 잠자코 지켜볼 걸 그랬나.

147|문득 그런 생각이 들었지만, 계속 이야기를 듣고 있자니 동치미 국물 없이 고구마를 백 개를 처먹은 기분이라 더는 참을 수가 없다.
148|
149|나는 푹신한 소파에 등을 기대며 입을 열었다.
150|
151|“솔직히 딱 까놓고 말해서 곧 공개될 마나 연공법 때문에 온 거잖아. 적당한 선에서 멈춰라. 여기서 더 가면 재미없다. 크로노스 같은 다른 거대 길드랑 손잡고 너희 담가 버릴 수 있으니까 나대지 마라. 지금 하고 싶은 말이 그거 아니야.”

153|“…….”

155|“아니, 시부럴. 서로 다 아는 처지에 뭐 이렇게 이리저리 돌려 말해요, 머리 아프게. 어차피 우리가 녹취하는 것도 아닌데 할 말만 하고 돌아가면 되지. 안 그래?”

157|폭포수처럼 쏟아지는 내 말을 말없이 듣고 있던 후긴이 문득 최 팀장을 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
158|
159|“혹여 예의에 어긋나는 것이 아닌가 싶어 말씀드리지 않았는데, 미스터 진께서 꼭 이 자리에 계셔야 할 이유가 있을까요?”
160|
161|“물론입니다.”
162|
163|최 팀장이 담담하게 대꾸했다.
164|
165|“진태경 씨는 그만큼 중요한 사람이니까요. 그리고 독대를 원하셨다면 처음부터 그리 말씀하셨어야 했습니다.”
166|
167|“그럼 지금부터라도 독대를 부탁드려도 되겠습니까?”
168|
169|“거절합니다.”
170|
171|한 치의 망설임도 없는 최 팀장의 대답에, 후긴이 황금빛 눈동자를 깜빡였다.
172|
173|“이거 참…… 당혹스럽군요.”
174|
175|“그건 우리 역시 마찬가집니다. 사전에 약속을 잡으셨다면 충분히 여러 부분을 조율할 수 있었을 텐데요.”
176|
177|“흠.”

179|외알 안경을 매만진 후긴이 입을 열었다.
180|
181|“그럼 제가 먼저 무례를 범한 셈이니, 정식으로 두 분께 사과드리겠습니다.”
182|
183|이놈 보게.
184|
185|처음에는 무슨 까마귀 컨셉인가 했는데, 괜히 신사 복장을 차려입은 게 아니다.
186|
187|제법 깍듯한 후긴의 태도에 나 역시 신사답게 대답했다.
188|
189|“그럼 그쪽이 먼저 잘못한 거니까, 전 사과 안 할게요.”
190|
191|“…….”
192|
193|“마음은 이미 알겠으니까 그렇게 쳐다보지 마시고. 아까 말했던 대로 진솔하게 대화나 나눠 봅시다. 오케이?”
194|
195|후우.
196|
197|후긴이 한숨과 함께 고개를 끄덕였다.
198|
199|“좋습니다. 이렇게까지 나오시니, 저도 단도직입적으로 말씀드릴 수밖에 없겠군요.”
200|
201|“짧게. 본론만.”
202|
203|집무실에 설치된 조명 마법 아래에서 후긴의 외알 안경이 반짝 빛난다.
204|
205|짧은 침묵은 금방 깨졌다. 말없이 나와 최 팀장을 응시하던 그가 입을 열었다.
206|
207|“마나 연공법 공개를 중단하십시오. 이 제안을 거절할 시 불이익이 있을 겁니다.”
208|
209|그것은 짧게 본론만 이야기하라는 내 요구를 백 퍼센트 충족시키는 한마디였고, 생각했던 것 이상으로 우리의 기분을 더럽게 만들었다.
210|
211|“뭐, 이미 짐작은 하고 있었는데…… 막상 이렇게 들으니까 엿 같네. 안 그래요?”
212|
213|내 물음에 최 팀장이 어깨를 으쓱했다.
214|
215|“그래도 조금 전처럼 몇 바퀴 돌려서 말하는 것보다는 훨씬 낫지 않습니까.”
216|
217|“그건 그래. 이번에도 아까처럼 말했으면 그땐 진짜…….”
218|
219|“참으셔야 합니다.”
220|
221|“굳이 최 팀장님이 안 말려도 참았어요. 일 키우기는 싫으니까. 근데 일단 안경은 벗으라고 했을 것 같아.”
222|
223|내 대답을 들은 최 팀장이 피식 웃었고, 후긴의 눈매가 가늘어졌다.
224|
225|“매우 무례하시군요. 듣던 대로.”
226|
227|“그러는 그쪽도 굉장히 불쾌하게 나오시네. 듣도 보도 못했는데.”
228|
229|“당장 이 자리에서 무력시위라도 할 생각입니까?”
230|
231|“필요하면 해야지. 아저씨가 안경 벗으면.”
232|
233|“……이보십시오, 미스터 진.”
234|
235|“네, 여보세요. 말씀하세요.”
236|
237|“흥분하지 마십시오. 이건 단지 제안입니다.”
238|
239|“입이 비뚤어졌어도 말은 똑바로 해야지. 내 귀에는 제안이 아니라 협박으로 들리는데.”
240|
241|“협박으로 들으셨다면, 정말 그렇게 될 수도 있겠지요. 하지만 제게 중요한 건 당신의 생각이 아닙니다.”
242|
243|단호하게 대답한 후긴이 최 팀장을 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
244|
245|“어찌하시겠습니까? 미스터 최.”
246|
247|차갑게 빛나는 황금빛 눈동자. 후긴의 입술 사이로 힘이 실린 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
248|
249|“선택하십시오. 당신이 직접.”
250|
251|

255|
256|
257|후긴은 확신하고 있었다.
258|
259|‘이건 거절할 수 없는 제안이다.’
260|
261|사실상의 최후통첩.
262|

A giant powerful enough to send a mere messenger to Ares Guild’s new master.

[P32]
“I’ve come today to convey the Guild Master’s congratulations.”

[P33]
Team Leader Choi’s expression remained calm.

[P34]
“Is that so?”

[P35]
“Yes. He is delighted to see a capable young man with all the right qualifications take charge of Ares Guild.”

[P36]
It sounded like praise. It wasn’t.

[P37]
I ran my tongue over my lips.

[P38]
*Well, look at these bastards…*

[P39]
Some things showed through no matter how much wrapping you piled on. Huginn’s courteous tone and manner couldn’t hide what lay beneath them.

[P40]
*Looking down on us from the start.*

[P41]
I felt as if we were receiving an envoy from an overlord state. Team Leader Choi wasn’t too stupid to notice, or rash enough to show his displeasure openly.

[P42]
“That is rather high praise while my maternal grandfather is still with us, but I’m grateful nonetheless. Grateful enough to want to thank him in person.”

[P43]
Huginn kept smiling despite the barb.

[P44]
“Ah, he was very sorry he could not come himself.”

[P45]
“The Guild Master must be busy. I’d heard he had withdrawn from public life several years ago… but it seems you can’t trust rumors.”

[P46]
The higher someone rose, the harder it became to get them out of their seat. That was an eternal truth. Cheon Taemin, who had reportedly vanished altogether, was simply an extreme case.

[P47]
Most major Guild Masters limited their contact with the outside world. Odin’s Guild Master was no different.

[P48]
“I’ve always respected him, so I would like to pay him a visit and introduce myself. What do you think?”

[P49]
“Haha. Well…”

[P50]
Huginn laughed aloud and laced his fingers together.

[P51]
“I’m sorry, but he has been so busy lately that I doubt it would be possible.”

[P52]
“It sounds as though something has happened.”

[P53]
“Yes. A minor matter, though quite troublesome in its way. He seems to be giving a great deal of thought to how he should handle it. The others are, too.”

[P54]
“The others?”

[P55]
“Acquaintances he has known for many years. The person he is meeting today is from Kronos… Ah, my apologies. I shouldn’t have said that.”

[P56]
The name of another major Guild—one of the world’s Ten Great Guilds alongside Ares—had slipped out.

[P57]
Team Leader Choi spoke quietly. “Kronos Guild.”

[P58]
“I would appreciate it if you could forget you heard that. I make mistakes like this from time to time, and the Guild Master calls me in for a reprimand.”

[P59]
The troubled look on Huginn’s face made me let out a short laugh.

[P60]
“What mistake?”

[P61]
“Pardon?”

[P62]
“Mr. Crow, drop the half-assed acting. Let’s talk honestly.”

[P63]
*Hmm. Maybe I should’ve kept my mouth shut.*

[P64]
But listening to him felt like choking down a hundred sweet potatoes without a drop of dongchimi broth to wash them down.[^1] I couldn’t take it anymore.

[P65]
I leaned back into the plush sofa.

[P66]
“Let’s be blunt. You’re here because the Mana Cultivation Method is about to go public. You want us to stop while we can, because if we take this any further, it won’t be fun. You and other major Guilds like Kronos can join forces and bury us, so we’d better not get cocky. That about cover it?”

[P67]
“……”

[P68]
“Fuck’s sake. We all know what this is about, so why give ourselves headaches talking in circles? We’re not recording you. Say what you came to say and go. Right?”

[P69]
Huginn listened to the whole torrent without a word, then turned to Team Leader Choi.

[P70]
“I hesitated to mention this for fear of being discourteous, but must Mr. Jin be present?”

[P71]
“Of course.”

[P72]
Team Leader Choi’s reply was calm.

[P73]
“Mr. Jin is that important. And if you wanted to speak with me alone, you should have said so at the outset.”

[P74]
“Then may I ask to speak with you alone now?”

[P75]
“No.”

[P76]
There wasn’t a moment’s hesitation in Team Leader Choi’s answer. Huginn blinked his golden eyes.

[P77]
“Well… this is awkward.”

[P78]
“We feel the same. Had you made an appointment, we could have arranged any number of things beforehand.”

[P79]
“Hm.”

[P80]
Huginn adjusted his monocle.

[P81]
“Since I was the first to be rude, I owe you both a formal apology.”

[P82]
*Would you look at him.*

[P83]
I’d thought the crow getup was just a gimmick, but apparently he hadn’t dressed like a gentleman for nothing. Since Huginn was being so courteous, I answered like a gentleman myself.

[P84]
“You were rude first, so I’m not apologizing.”

[P85]
“……”

[P86]
“I know what you want, so stop staring at me. Like I said, let’s talk honestly. Okay?”

[P87]
Huginn sighed and nodded.

[P88]
“Very well. Since you insist, I shall be direct.”

[P89]
“Keep it short. Get to the point.”

[P90]
Huginn’s monocle flashed beneath the office’s lighting Magic. The silence lasted only a moment before he spoke.

[P91]
“Stop the release of the Mana Cultivation Method. If you refuse, there will be consequences.”

[P92]
He had done exactly as I’d asked. Somehow, hearing it put so plainly felt even shittier than I’d expected.

[P93]
“Well, I figured that was coming, but… fuck, it’s unpleasant to hear. Don’t you think?”

[P94]
Team Leader Choi shrugged.

[P95]
“Isn’t it better than listening to him talk in circles again?”

[P96]
“That’s true. If he’d done that one more time, I really would’ve…”

[P97]
“You must control yourself.”

[P98]
“I was going to, even without you telling me. I don’t want to make this a bigger problem. Though I probably would’ve told him to take off the monocle first.”

[P99]
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh. Huginn’s eyes narrowed.

[P100]
“You are every bit as rude as I was told.”

[P101]
“And you’re every bit as unpleasant as I’d expect from someone I’ve never heard of.”

[P102]
“Do you intend to make a show of force here?”

[P103]
“If I have to. Once you take off that monocle.”

[P104]
“……Mr. Jin.”

[P105]
“Yes, hello? Go ahead.”

[P106]
“Do not lose your temper. This is merely a proposal.”

[P107]
“Call it what it is. Sounds like a threat to me.”

[P108]
“If you choose to hear it as a threat, it may well become one. But your opinion is not what matters to me.”

[P109]
Huginn turned to Team Leader Choi.

[P110]
“What will you do, Mr. Choi?”

[P111]
His golden eyes gleamed coldly. His next words carried weight.

[P112]
“Make the choice yourself.”

[P113]
* * *

[P114]
Huginn was certain.

[P115]
*He can’t refuse this.*

[P116]
It was an ultimatum in all but name. Anyone with the slightest sense would back down.

[P117]
Jin Taekyung was unpredictable to the point of being half-mad. But the young Asian man before Huginn, Choi Minwoo, would make a different choice.

[P118]
Besides…

[P119]
*The Slayer won’t intervene. Master said so. That makes it a fact.*

[P120]
The assurance had come from the one man to whom Huginn gave his absolute loyalty. His Master had never been wrong. Choi Minwoo’s answer was as good as decided.

[P121]
Perhaps that was why his response, when it came, sounded only natural.

[P122]
“Since things have come to this, I suppose I have no choice. All right.”

[P123]
“As expected. You are a wise man, Mr. Choi.”

[P124]
Huginn felt his composure returning after his exchange with Jin Taekyung. He recovered his smile.

[P125]
“Then I may take it that tomorrow evening’s release of the Mana Cultivation Method has been canceled entirely?”

[P126]
“Of course. I’ve changed my mind.”

[P127]
“Excellent. He will be pleased to hear it.”

[P128]
Huginn rose and added, “As will the others.”

[P129]
“I hope so,” Choi Minwoo said.

[P130]
“They are reasonable people. I’m sure we can build a good relationship in a more amicable atmosphere from now on.”

[P131]
With that pointed remark, Huginn looked at Jin Taekyung.

[P132]
Only moments ago, Jin had been spouting vulgarities to his face. Now he was practically lying back on the sofa, fiddling with his smartphone.

[P133]
*Rude to the very end.*

[P134]
But satisfaction outweighed Huginn’s annoyance. He had won.

[P135]
Before leaving, he adjusted his silk hat like the cultured gentleman he was and offered Jin his hand.

[P136]
“Mr. Jin, I was discourteous today, though I did not intend to be. I hope we can meet with smiles next time.”

[P137]
Only a winner had the privilege of mocking the loser with kind words. When Jin refused his hand and gave a curt reply instead, Huginn felt better still.

[P138]
“You’re in a hurry. It hasn’t even finished uploading.”

[P139]
“I have an urgent matter to attend to. Good day.”

[P140]
His business here was done. Huginn gave Choi Minwoo a polite nod, turned, and headed for the door.

[P141]
Step. Step.

[P142]
His footsteps were light on the carpet. At the door, he stopped.

[P143]
He couldn’t ignore what Jin had just said.

[P144]
“Did you say…?”

[P145]
Huginn turned back, his words trailing off. He stared at Jin as if he couldn’t believe it.

[P146]
Jin blinked.

[P147]
“Hm? Oh, uploading?”

[P148]
“Uploading…?”

[P149]
“Yeah. It’s nothing important. You should get going—you look busy.”

[P150]
*Uploading. Uploading. Uploading.*

[P151]
The word throbbed in Huginn’s ears in time with his heartbeat.

[P152]
“What. Exactly. Did you. Upload?”

[P153]
It was Choi Minwoo, not Jin Taekyung, who answered.

[P154]
“Didn’t I tell you? I changed my mind.”

[P155]
“Surely not.”

[P156]
“The Mana Cultivation Method. We’ve decided to release it today.”

[P157]
“……!”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
